cards.explanation: The answer is that Peter follows at a distance. Luke says, "And Peter followed at a distance." He's not gone, but he's not up close either. I think he's trying to stay near without standing out.
The answer is that she says he was with Jesus. She looks at him intently as he sits in the firelight. Then she says, "This man also was with Him…" She means Jesus, the One who was just seized.

The answer is False. The servant girl says Peter was with Jesus, and Peter answers, "Woman, I do not know Him…" She asks about being with Jesus, and he says he doesn't even know Him. That's the first of three times in this courtyard that Peter denies it.
The answer is True. Luke says someone else saw Peter and said, "You also are one of them." Peter answered, "Man, I am not." That's two for two, friends. He's not even leaving the door cracked.

The answer is that Peter is a Galilean too. The man insists, "Certainly this man was with Him, for he too is a Galilean." Galilee is the region Jesus is from, and the man says Peter is from there too. That's his whole case, and he says it like he's got proof.

The answer is that the rooster crows. Luke says, "And immediately, while he was still speaking, the rooster crowed." It crows right while Peter is still talking. That timing is something, friends. That rooster showed up like it had a meeting on the calendar.
The answer is True. Luke says, "And the Lord turned and looked at Peter." Jesus is the Lord here. The text gives us the look, and then Luke says Peter remembers the word the Lord had spoken to him.

The answer is three. The Lord told Peter, "Before the rooster crows today, you will deny Me three times." Count them in the courtyard: the servant girl, then someone else, then another man. That's three, just like the Lord said.

The answer is weeps. Luke says, "And he went outside and wept bitterly." Peter remembers the Lord's words, and then he goes out and weeps. I think this is one of the saddest moments in the whole story. No joke from me here, friends.

The answer is that they demand He prophesy who hit Him. The men blindfold Him and keep demanding, "Prophesy! Who hit You?" They're mocking Him while they hit Him. It's a hard scene, friends. I'll let Luke's words stand.

The answer is True. Luke says, "At daybreak the council of the elders of the people, both the chief priests and scribes, met together." The night is over, and the council gathers. Daybreak is when they meet together.

The answer is the chief priests and scribes. Luke says the council of the elders of the people is made up of "…both the chief priests and scribes…" They meet together at daybreak. Then they lead Jesus into their Sanhedrin.
The answer is False. The council says, "If You are the Christ, tell us." Jesus answers, "If I tell you, you will not believe." Believing is the very thing He says isn't coming.

The answer is that they will not answer. Jesus says, "And if I ask you a question, you will not answer." So whether He tells them or asks them, He says it won't go anywhere. It's a quiet line, friends, and Luke leaves it as it is.

The answer is that they ask if He is the Son of God. After Jesus speaks of the Son of Man, the whole council asks, "Are You then the Son of God?" Luke says they all asked Him that. Jesus replies, "You say that I am."

The answer is False. The council says, "Why do we need any more testimony? We have heard it for ourselves from His own lips." They say they're done needing testimony. They believe they've heard enough.
